# Tooltip

Figma: [04d. Tooltip](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-914) · Family: 04 Data Display · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-06-02

A transient information bubble that appears on hover or focus, pointing back to its trigger element via a small arrow. Light bubble with subtle border, drop shadow for elevation, optional leading info icon. Used for icon hints, label clarification, and short explanatory copy. Three axes beyond placement and direction: Size (sm/md), HasTitle (title + body or body only), and HasIcon (info icon at the start of the text - swappable via the icon prop).

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/tooltip/reference.png`

### Tooltip

Light bordered bubble with an arrow that appears on hover, focus or long-press to explain an icon, term or number. Supplementary only and never interactive.

Level: molecule · Part of: KeyValue

Use when:
- Defining a financial term such as Sukuk or net return next to a label
- Explaining how expected return or a fee is calculated (Size=md with title)
- Naming an icon-only IconButton
- Clarifying an info icon on a KeyValue row

Don't use when:
- Content with a link, button or form: use Popover
- Information the investor must see to decide (fees, risk, minimum): show it inline or with Alert
- Form validation errors: use the Form Field error state and Form Field Helper
- Rich explanations on mobile: use BottomSheet
- Hover readouts inside charts: use Chart / ChartTooltip

Accessibility: role=tooltip linked by aria-describedby; show on keyboard focus and long-press; never hide critical info in it.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Tooltips reveal supplementary information on hover or focus - never as primary content. They're for situations where a user needs more context but the screen would feel cluttered if that context were always visible: icon-only buttons that don't self-explain, technical terms, abbreviations, status indicators that benefit from a "what does this mean?" affordance.

Three structural axes beyond placement and direction. Size (sm for one-line label tooltips, md for explanatory tooltips with optional title), HasTitle (title + body or body only), and HasIcon (leading info icon - swappable per instance via the `icon` property to match the context - warning triangle for cautions, lightbulb for tips, etc).

### Family at a glance

> **Warning:** Tooltips are for SUPPLEMENTARY information only. If a user must see the information to use the interface, it does NOT belong in a tooltip. Tooltips don't appear on touch devices the same way (no hover state), so any information critical to the task must be visible without hovering.

### Anatomy

Every tooltip is a bordered light bubble + a directional arrow + drop shadow for elevation. The arrow uses a custom vector path that draws only its two slanted edges as stroke (not the base), so the bubble border breaks cleanly at the join point and the arrow visually feels like an extension of the bubble.

Bubble

Light bg/elevated fill with 1px border/default stroke (inset). Rounded corners (Radius/4 for sm, Radius/8 for md). Vertical auto-layout containing an optional title row (with optional leading icon) and the body. Max-width 200 for sm, 280 for md - body wraps inside. Text in text/default for maximum contrast.

Arrow

Triangular vector with the same bg/elevated fill. The stroke is only on the two slanted edges (open path, not the base) so the bubble border breaks cleanly at the arrow base instead of crossing through it. 10×6 for sm, 12×7 for md. Path orientation flips based on Placement so the apex always points toward the trigger.

Shadow

Shadow/sm effect (0/2 offset, 4 blur, 10% black) applied to the wrapping component frame so both bubble AND arrow cast the shadow together. This gives the tooltip elevation against any light page background - surface, base, or elevated - without needing a heavier outline.

Icon (optional)

When HasIcon=true, a 14px (sm) or 16px (md) info icon leads the title or body row. Defaults to Icon/info from Syntropy Icons. The `icon` component property is INSTANCE_SWAP - designers swap it per-instance to match context (warning triangle, lightbulb, question mark, etc). Icon color inherits from its own design system bindings; no override needed.

### Placement - choosing which side

Placement picks which side of the trigger the tooltip appears on. The arrow always points back at the trigger, so the wrong placement produces a tooltip whose arrow points off into empty space. Pick placement based on (1) which direction has room without clipping at viewport edges, and (2) where the user's focus is likely to land after seeing the tooltip.

Placement = top

DEFAULT for most icon buttons in toolbars, headers, and form labels. Tooltip floats above the trigger; user's eye moves UP slightly to read. Avoid when trigger is near the top viewport edge.

Placement = right

Use for form field labels, settings rows, list items. Tooltip floats to the right; works well when there's a column of triggers on the left side of the screen. In RTL layouts, swap to LEFT.

Placement = bottom

Use when trigger is near the top of the viewport (e.g. app bar icons, nav menu items). Common in navigation. User's eye moves DOWN - natural for items at the top.

Placement = left

Use for triggers in the right column of a layout, or in RTL where you'd otherwise use right. Less common - most users scan left-to-right (or right-to-left in RTL), so right-side placement feels more natural by default.

> **Tip:** Smart placement at runtime: in code, the tooltip's effective placement should auto-flip if the chosen direction would cause viewport clipping. E.g. Placement=top requested, but trigger is 8px from the top of the viewport → swap to Placement=bottom at render time. The Figma component encodes the visual design for each placement; runtime logic picks the right one.

### Size - sm vs md

Two sizes cover the two real-world use cases. Choosing the wrong size makes the tooltip feel either too cramped (sm for explanatory copy) or too prominent (md for a one-line icon hint).

Size = sm

· Padding 8 / 10 · Radius 4 · Arrow 10 × 6

· Body 12 / 16 · Title (if present) 13 / 16

· Max width 200 · Icon 14px (when shown)

· Use for: icon-button hints, abbreviation tooltips, status indicator labels - one line, one purpose

Size = md

· Padding 12 / 16 · Radius 8 · Arrow 12 × 7

· Body 13 / 18 · Title (if present) 14 / 20

· Max width 280 · Icon 16px (when shown)

· Use for: explanatory tooltips with title + 1-3 sentences - financial term definitions, "what does this calculation mean", investment caveats

### Icon - leading visual cue

When HasIcon=true, an icon leads the title row (or body row if there's no title). The icon is an INSTANCE_SWAP component property named `icon` - designers swap it per instance to match the context. The default is Icon/info from Syntropy Icons, but warning triangle for cautions, lightbulb for tips, calculator for financial-calculation tooltips, etc. are all valid swaps.

### 

> **Tip:** In RTL mode, the icon swaps to the trailing edge (right side) of the text row - visually correct for right-to-left reading. The auto-layout handles this automatically based on the Direction variant; no per-instance configuration needed.

> **Info:** When HasIcon=false, the icon slot is omitted entirely (not just hidden). Text aligns flush to the bubble padding edge. Switching HasIcon between true and false re-flows the layout cleanly - no jarring gaps.

### Direction - LTR + RTL

Every variant exists in LTR (English, IBM Plex Sans) and RTL (Arabic, Noto Sans Arabic) directions. Like the rest of Syntropy, Arabic uses Noto Sans because IBM Plex Sans Arabic is not installed in this Figma file. Text aligns to the start edge - left in LTR, right in RTL. The icon (when present) also moves to the start edge automatically.

> **Warning:** Font fallback (same as Badge): Noto Sans Arabic Medium is used for all Arabic variants because IBM Plex Sans Arabic is not installed in this Figma file. If IBM Plex Sans Arabic is added later, regenerate all RTL variants for visual consistency with the LTR variants.

### Content guidance

Tooltips fail when they hold the wrong kind of content. Keeping the bar high here protects users from hidden critical information and from cognitive overload.

### When to use a tooltip

- Naming an icon-only button: "Mute notifications", "Copy link", "Add to portfolio".
- Defining a technical term in context: "Sukuk - Sharia-compliant fixed-income instrument representing fractional ownership of an asset."
- Explaining a number, percentage, or calculation: "Expected annual return based on 6 historical comparable issuances. Past performance does not guarantee future results."
- Clarifying a status indicator: hover the badge "Late" to see "Day 30+ · recovery against guarantees started."
- Disambiguating an abbreviation: "ROI · Return on Investment".

### When NOT to use a tooltip

- Critical information the user MUST see to use the interface. Tooltips don't appear on touch devices the same way; if it matters, make it visible.
- Form validation errors. These belong in the form field's error state, not a tooltip.
- Interactive content - links, buttons, scrolling content. Use Popover/Modal/BottomSheet instead.
- Long-form content. If you need 4+ lines, you need a different surface: an inline expandable section, a side panel, or a dedicated page.
- Decorative or redundant. If a button is labeled "Save", a tooltip saying "Save" is noise.

### Length limits

- Size = sm: stay to a single line. About 30 characters for English, 25 for Arabic. If you must wrap, reconsider; sm is for labels, not sentences.
- Size = md: aim for 1-2 sentences of body, optionally preceded by a title. Hard ceiling: 4 lines of body. If you need more, the content does not belong in a tooltip.
- Title (when used): single short noun phrase. "Investment minimum", not "About the minimum amount required to invest in this issuance."

### Icon usage

- Default icon (Icon/info) signals "general informational tooltip". Use as-is for most tooltips that explain a concept or term.
- Swap to a warning triangle (Icon/triangle-warning) for tooltips that warn about consequences - e.g. "This action cannot be undone."
- Swap to a lightbulb (Icon/lightbulb) for tips and best practices - e.g. "Pro tip: enable auto-renewal to lock in current rates."
- Swap to a question mark (Icon/help-circle) for "what is this?" explanations - typically paired with a small clickable element.
- Skip the icon entirely (HasIcon=false) when the text alone communicates the meaning and an icon would be noise - e.g. one-word labels on icon buttons.

### Code examples - Flutter

Reference implementations. Real production code lives in lib/design_system/tooltip/.

### Basic usage

```dart
// Wrap any focusable widget in a Tooltip for hover/focus/long-press behavior.
SafqahTooltip(
  message: 'Investment minimum',
  child: IconButton(
    icon: Icon(Icons.info_outline),
    onPressed: null,
  ),
)

// With title + body (md size):
SafqahTooltip(
  title: 'Investment minimum',
  message: 'You can start with 1,000 SAR. There is no upper limit for this issuance.',
  size: TooltipSize.md,
  child: Icon(Icons.help_outline),
)

// With leading icon:
SafqahTooltip(
  title: 'Investment minimum',
  message: 'You can start with 1,000 SAR.',
  size: TooltipSize.md,
  leadingIcon: SyntropyIcons.info,  // or .triangleWarning, .lightbulb, .helpCircle
  child: Icon(Icons.attach_money),
)
```

### Runtime placement auto-flip

```dart
// File: lib/design_system/tooltip/placement_resolver.dart
// Choose the best placement at runtime based on viewport space.
// If requested placement would clip the tooltip, flip to the opposite side.
class TooltipPlacementResolver {
  static TooltipPlacement resolve({
    required TooltipPlacement requested,
    required Rect triggerRect,
    required Size tooltipSize,
    required Size viewportSize,
    double padding = 8.0,
  }) {
    // Check if requested placement has enough space
    final hasSpace = _hasSpaceFor(requested, triggerRect, tooltipSize, viewportSize, padding);
    if (hasSpace) return requested;

    // Try opposite placement
    final opposite = _opposite(requested);
    if (_hasSpaceFor(opposite, triggerRect, tooltipSize, viewportSize, padding)) {
      return opposite;
    }

    // Try perpendicular placements
    for (final placement in _perpendiculars(requested)) {
      if (_hasSpaceFor(placement, triggerRect, tooltipSize, viewportSize, padding)) {
        return placement;
      }
    }

    // Fall back to requested even if it clips - better than no tooltip
    return requested;
  }

  static TooltipPlacement _opposite(TooltipPlacement p) {
    switch (p) {
      case TooltipPlacement.top:    return TooltipPlacement.bottom;
      case TooltipPlacement.bottom: return TooltipPlacement.top;
      case TooltipPlacement.left:   return TooltipPlacement.right;
      case TooltipPlacement.right:  return TooltipPlacement.left;
    }
  }
}
```

### Long-press for touch devices

```dart
// SafqahTooltip wraps Flutter's built-in Tooltip widget, which handles long-press
// automatically on touch devices. The hover/focus behavior is layered on top.
class SafqahTooltip extends StatelessWidget {
  final String message;
  final String? title;
  final IconData? leadingIcon;
  final TooltipSize size;
  final TooltipPlacement preferredPlacement;
  final Widget child;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Tooltip(
      message: title != null ? '$title\n$message' : message,
      preferBelow: preferredPlacement == TooltipPlacement.bottom,
      richMessage: title != null
        ? _buildRichMessage(context)
        : null,
      decoration: _buildDecoration(),
      padding: _paddingForSize(size),
      waitDuration: const Duration(milliseconds: 500),
      child: child,
    );
  }
}
```

### Do and Don't

Four pairs of operational guidance for tooltip usage.

### Use tooltips for supplementary information only

- **Do** · Scenario name: Use a tooltip to clarify an icon button: "Mute notifications" on a bell icon. The button is still usable without seeing the tooltip; the label just speeds up recognition.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Never put critical information in a tooltip. Touch users may not see it, screen-reader users may not encounter it in the expected order, and users in a hurry will skip it.

### Keep tooltips short

- **Do** · Scenario name: sm size: one line, ~30 chars in English. md size: 1-2 short sentences, optionally with a title. Cut every word that doesn't add meaning.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't use a tooltip for 3+ sentences of explanation. If it doesn't fit in 4 lines of body text, the content belongs in a different surface - an inline expandable section, side panel, or dedicated page.

### Match icon to meaning

- **Do** · Scenario name: Use the default Icon/info for neutral explanations. Swap to warning triangle for cautions, lightbulb for tips, question mark for "what is this?". The icon prop is INSTANCE_SWAP - change it per-instance to fit the context.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't use HasIcon=true with the default info icon when the icon adds no meaning. If text alone is enough, skip the icon entirely (HasIcon=false) - unnecessary icons are visual noise.

### Never put interactive content inside

- **Do** · Scenario name: Body text only. If users need to click "Learn more" or follow a link, the right pattern is a Popover (focusable content) or a navigation link in the surrounding UI.
- **Don't** · Scenario name: Don't embed buttons, links, or form controls inside a tooltip. ARIA role="tooltip" doesn't reliably announce interactive descendants, and the hover/blur dismiss behavior makes them unreachable on touch.

### Notes from the maintainer

Design decisions, known gaps, and constraints for the next maintainer.

> **Info:** Light bubble + border + shadow (canonical styling). Switched from the original dark inverse styling because (1) it integrates better with most product surfaces that use light backgrounds, (2) the border + shadow give cleaner definition than relying on a dark fill, (3) the icon reads more cleanly in dark-on-light. The earlier dark version is preserved in the file Changelog if it ever needs comparison.

> **Tip:** Arrow uses custom vector with 2-edge stroke. The standard figma.createPolygon() draws a stroke on ALL edges, which would visibly cross the bubble border at the join point. The custom vector instead draws TWO open paths: a closed triangle for the fill, and an open path along only the two slanted edges for the stroke. Combined with itemSpacing=-1 overlap, this gives a perfectly clean visual join.

> **Info:** Icon is INSTANCE_SWAP, not a variant. The HasIcon axis is a boolean (icon present or not) but WHICH icon is shown is a separate component property (`icon`). This means you can have HasIcon=true variants with any icon - info (default), warning, lightbulb, help, etc. Don't add icon-specific variants like "HasIcon=warning" - use the swap.

> **Info:** Icon color inherits from the icon component's own bindings. The info icon has its internal vectors bound to icon/default - when placed inside the tooltip, it picks up the default icon color naturally. If you swap to an icon with different color bindings, it will use those. No per-tooltip color override needed (or available).

> **Info:** Runtime placement is the calling code's job. The Figma component encodes the 4 visual placements; the calling code decides which one to use based on viewport space. A TooltipPlacementResolver class in lib/design_system/tooltip/ handles auto-flip when the chosen placement would clip at the viewport edge. See Code Examples section.

> **Info:** No dark mode yet (same as Badge). Tooltips have Light-mode-only palettes. On dark page backgrounds the white bubble still reads correctly (high contrast), but a proper dark mode would need re-verification.

> **Info:** Arabic font fallback: Noto Sans Arabic Medium. Same constraint as the rest of Syntropy - IBM Plex Sans Arabic is not installed in this file. If installed later, regenerate all RTL variants.

> **Tip:** Hover delay must match Material 3 (500ms) for consistency with other Syntropy components. Keyboard focus shows the tooltip immediately. Touch devices use Flutter Tooltip's built-in long-press behavior - no custom code needed.

> **Warning:** Don't detach tooltip instances to customize copy. Use the message + title props on the Flutter widget instead. To customize the icon, use the `icon` INSTANCE_SWAP property. Detached instances break design system audit and create silent drift.
